title: an exported void assertion helper may abort with panic(...) and needs no Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type: 'Calling `panic(...)` MUST NOT force a function's return type to widen into `Result<A, Panic>`.' and 'A function that validates an argument, refuses a forgery, or asserts an invariant MUST therefore be able to abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type.' docs/DECISIONS.md carries the matching Locked entry ('Calling `panic(...)` does not widen a return type into `Result<A, Panic>` … the prohibition is on the compiler forcing it'). `E` is the expected-error channel (reference/function-channels.mdx) and a panic is not an expected error, so a construct that aborts with `panic(...)` keeps whatever return type it declares. The exported form matters on its own: an exported declaration is a public contract, and the rule that a public contract spells fallibility directly (docs/DECISIONS.md, Locked) used to reach this function through the panic. Measured SMITHERS1102 before the rule landed — a different diagnostic from the unexported forms, which is why this is a case rather than a variant. `void` is the return type an assertion helper wants and the one the widening made unwritable.
